body.statement:
Put \(q=Sd\).  Suppose \(\delta_0<1/2\),
\(c_\Sigma I_q\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_q\), and
\(\operatorname{dist}(z_{0s},\partial[0,1]^d)\ge\delta_0\) for every \(s\).
For every \(\eta\in(0,1)\) and every fixed \(\epsilon_4>0\), there are
constants \(c_\eta>0\) and \(N_\eta<\infty\), depending only on
\(\eta,\epsilon_4\) and the fixed class parameters, such that for every
\(N\ge N_\eta\) there are finite-support probability laws \(G_0,G_1\) on
\(\mathbb R^q\) with means \(z_0,z_1\), respectively, common exact
covariance \(\Sigma\), and
\[
 \mathbb E_{G_v}\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z-z_v)\|_2^4\le q^2+\epsilon_4,
 \qquad
 N\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(z_1-z_0)\|_2^2=c_\eta^2,
 \qquad v\in\{0,1\}.
\]
The displacement \(z_1-z_0\) has one nonzero coordinate, \(z_1\) obeys the
same \(\delta_0\)-interior restriction, and
\(\|G_1^{\otimes N}-G_0^{\otimes N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le1-\eta\).
body.justification: For every prescribed elliptic full covariance, a finite-support construction supplies an overlapping root-\(N\) location pair with arbitrarily small positive excess above the covariance-implied fourth-moment floor.
body.gap: The local \(\epsilon_4>0\) is witness slack at the Jensen boundary, not a model restriction.
body.consumer: Conditional, marginal, and honest donor converses use the pair at the required overlap level.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(q=Sd\).  Choose a signed coordinate vector \(e\) pointing toward
\(1/2\) and set
\[
 w=\frac{\Sigma^{-1/2}e}{\|\Sigma^{-1/2}e\|_2}.
\]
Let \(O\) be orthogonal with first column \(w\).  Since \(B^4>q^2\), choose
\(\epsilon\in(0,B^4-q^2)\), put \(a=(1+\epsilon)^{1/2}>1\), and, for
\(|u|\) small, define \(A_u\in\{-a,0,a\}\) by
\[
 p_+(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a^2}+\frac{u}{2a},\quad
 p_-(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a^2}-\frac{u}{2a},\quad
 p_0(u)=1-\frac{1+u^2}{a^2}.                                \tag{1}
\]
All three probabilities are positive near zero, and direct summation gives
\[
 \mathbb EA_u=u,\qquad \mathbb EA_u^2=1+u^2,
 \qquad\operatorname{Var}(A_u)=1.                           \tag{2}
\]
Let \(R_2,\ldots,R_q\) be independent Rademacher variables, independent of
\(A_u\), and set \(V_u=O(A_u,R_2,\ldots,R_q)^\top\).  Then
\[
 \mathbb EV_u=uw,\qquad\operatorname{Var}(V_u)=I_q,          \tag{3}
\]
and orthogonal invariance gives
\[
 \mathbb E\|V_u-uw\|_2^4
 =\mathbb E(A_u-u)^4+2(q-1)+(q-1)^2.                        \tag{4}
\]
At zero the right side is
\(a^2+2(q-1)+(q-1)^2=q^2+\epsilon<B^4\).  It is continuous in \(u\), so
it remains at most \(B^4\) after shrinking the neighborhood.

Let \(G_u\) be the law of \(Z_u=z_0+\Sigma^{1/2}V_u\).  Equations (3)--(4)
give
\[
 z(u):=\mathbb EZ_u
 =z_0+\frac{u}{\|\Sigma^{-1/2}e\|_2}e,\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(Z_u)=\Sigma,                            \tag{5}
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_u-z(u))\|_2^4\le B^4.          \tag{6}
\]
The Hellinger affinity between \(G_0\) and \(G_u\) is
\(a_H(u)=\sum_{r\in\{-,0,+\}}\{p_r(0)p_r(u)\}^{1/2}\).
The probabilities in (1) stay bounded away from zero near zero, so
\(a_H''\) is bounded there; also \(a_H(0)=1\) and
\(a_H'(0)=\tfrac12\sum_rp_r'(0)=0\).  Taylor's formula therefore gives
\[
 a_H(u)\ge1-Cu^2.                                            \tag{7}
\]
For \(CNu^2\le1/2\), product factorization and
\(1-x\ge e^{-2x}\) give \(a_H(u)^N\ge e^{-2CNu^2}\).  For dominated
laws, Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \|P-G\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\left\{1-\left(\int\sqrt{dP\,dG}\right)^2\right\}^{1/2}. \tag{8}
\]
Choose \(c_\eta>0\) small enough that (7)--(8), with
\(u=c_\eta N^{-1/2}\), make the product total variation at most
\(1-\eta\).  Reduce \(c_\eta\) so it is in the moment neighborhood and
\(c_\eta C_\Sigma^{1/2}\le1/2-\delta_0\).  Equation (5) then yields
\[
 N\|\Sigma^{-1/2}\{z(u)-z_0\}\|_2^2=c_\eta^2.              \tag{9}
\]
Moreover \(\|\Sigma^{-1/2}e\|_2^{-1}\le C_\Sigma^{1/2}\); hence the
one-coordinate displacement toward \(1/2\) preserves the interior
restriction.  Taking \(G_0=G_{u=0}\) and
\(G_1=G_{u=c_\eta N^{-1/2}}\) proves every assertion.
